statement: Prop 5 (manuscript eq. (13)), all n: if F_E is unsatisfiable, A_E z = 1 is solvable over F_3, and deleting any single clause makes F_E satisfiable, then the rows of A_E (restricted to the n' occurring variables) are linearly independent over F_3, so rank = |E| and |E| <= n'-1.
derivation: (1) Any F_3 dependence sum lambda_i r_i = 0 with lambda_j != 0 satisfies sum_{i != j} lambda_i = -lambda_j, using a solution z of A_E z = 1; hence every w satisfying the other rows also satisfies r_j.w = 1. (2) Minimality gives a Boolean x satisfying F_E minus clause j; then r_j.x = 1 mod 3, and since r_j.x is a sum of three 0/1 values in {0..3}, it equals 1, so x satisfies F_E, a contradiction. (3) The all-ones vector lies in ker A_E because each row sums to 3 = 0 mod 3, so dim ker >= 1 and |E| <= n'-1.

LEMMA Thm1-two-valued (manuscript eq. (3), all n>=3, E subset of T_n): F_E is satisfiable iff some z in A_E = {z in F_3^n : A_E z = 1} takes at most two values. Proof. (a) If x in {0,1}^n satisfies F_E, then each clause sum is an integer in {0..3} that is 1 mod 3, hence 1; so z = x in A_E has values in {0,1}. (b) Let z in A_E take at most two values, E nonempty (E empty: z=0). A constant value a gives clause sums 3a = 0 mod 3, not 1, so the value set is {0,1}, {0,2} or {1,2}. Case {0,1}: x = z is Boolean with clause sums 1. Case {0,2}: z = 2y, y Boolean; 2(y_a+y_b+y_c) = 1 mod 3 gives y_a+y_b+y_c = 2 exactly (range {0..3}); x = 1-y is Boolean with x_a+x_b+x_c = 1. Case {1,2}: z = 1+y; clause sum = 3 + (y_a+y_b+y_c) = 1 mod 3 gives sum y = 1 exactly; x = y. In each case x satisfies F_E. QED. Closes: none (reformulation, no open obligation).
